correctness.rationale: For every \(d\ge1\), \(1\le\ell\le d\), iid isotropic orthogonal frame and \(0<\alpha\lambda d/\ell<2\), exact quadratic expansion reduces the update to (I-beta R)x-a u. \(R^2=rR\), \(Ru=ru\), \(\|u\|_2^2=d\) and \(\mathbb E R=I\) give mean contraction \(1-\beta\) and squared-error contraction \(\rho=1-\beta(2-\beta r)\), strictly below one. Solving both recurrences gives the claimed limit, and Cauchy-Schwarz with E PP^T=I gives \(q\le\ell\). Explicit signed, unsigned and globally biased sign mixtures attain all q. A standalone exact-rational checker replayed 1305 finite conditional transitions, means and squared moments, including both sharp sample cases. These finite checks support but do not substitute the symbolic universal proof. Excluded stability endpoints and nonisotropic curvature are not asserted.

value.rationale: The result answers a natural algorithm-design gap: does symmetry-based cancellation of a forward-difference bias always minimize fixed-step stationary optimization risk? It supplies an exact sharp classification over all isotropic orthogonal-frame laws, not merely a selected test example. The phase reversal at normalized step one cleanly separates noise-induced variance from orientation-induced bias and yields dimension-uniform endpoint formulas and a reproducible rational example. It is a motivated structural boundary for published S-SZD parameter and direction choices, without claiming a general noisy/nonisotropic theorem.
